R22.place: El Capitan, Yosemite Valley, USA: USGS 3DEP 1 m blocks read by HTTP range requests from 10 km files; the tile is in two projects, the newer (2020) has no data here, so the 2019 one (an older file layout, not a COG) fills the blocks

R23.place: Moab Rim, Utah, USA: a 1 m tile in three projects; the blocks are composed from 2020 and 2018 (the 2022 project has no data here)

R24.place: Mount Juneau, Alaska, USA: no 1 m lidar near the centre, so --source auto takes Alaska's IfSAR DTM (5 m, cells in Alaska Albers)

R25.place: Martinswand near Innsbruck, Austria: BEV's ALS DTM and DSM, 1 m blocks read by HTTP range requests from the 50 km COGs of the 2025 edition, on a working grid in EPSG:3035
R25.notes: --source auto picks austria (the centre is in AT); first run on an empty cache: 9 blocks of 1 km per layer, about 2 MB each; every line crosses the forest below the wall (over_trees)

R26.place: Cheddar Gorge, England: the Environment Agency's LIDAR Composite DTM and first-return DSM 2022, 1 m tiles of 2 km from its WCS, on a working grid in British National Grid (EPSG:27700)
R26.notes: --source auto picks england (the centre is in GB-ENG); first run on an empty cache: 2 tiles of 2 km per layer, 16.8 MB each (uncompressed GeoTIFF from the WCS)

R27.place: Dinorwig slate quarries, Llanberis, Wales: the Welsh Government LiDAR 2020-22 DTM and DSM, 1 m blocks read by HTTP range requests from the two national COGs, on a working grid in British National Grid (EPSG:27700)
R27.notes: --source auto picks wales (the centre is in GB-WLS); quarry walls of 50-100 m spans; replaced Llanberis Pass (32 short lines) on 2026-11-01

R28.place: Hohenstein in the Süntel, Lower Saxony, Germany: LGLN's DGM1 and DOM1 1 m tiles from its STAC APIs (newest survey per 1 km tile)
R28.notes: --source auto picks lower_saxony (the centre is in DE-NI); first run on an empty cache: 9 tiles of 1 km per layer, about 5 MB each; the limestone wall above the forest: nearly every line crosses trees (over_trees)

R29.place: Bode gorge between the Rosstrappe and the Hexentanzplatz, Saxony-Anhalt, Germany: LVermGeo's DGM1 and DOM1 1 m from its WCS (2 km tiles, multipart answers with bare LF lines)
R29.notes: --source auto picks saxony_anhalt (the centre is in DE-ST); first run on an empty cache: 3 tiles of 2 km per layer, 16 MB each from the WCS (18 s); the 0.02 km² filled are the grid's corners outside the WCS tiles of the circle; nearly every line crosses the forest of the gorge (over_trees)

R30.place: Sella towers above Passo Sella, South Tyrol (IT-BZ): the province's DTM and DSM 2.5 m (LiDAR 2004-2006) from its GeoServer WCS, tiles on the coverage's half-pixel grid (origin 1.25 m), the part in Trentino filled from FABDEM
R30.notes: --source auto picks south_tyrol (the centre is in IT-BZ); first run on an empty cache: 2 tiles of 5 km per layer, DEFLATE-compressed by the server (1.4-8 MB each); the 3 pixels next to the province's edge (blended with zero) are dropped and filled from FABDEM (before: 18678 anchors, coverage 90.67%, the same lines); on steep rock the DSM stands metres above the DTM (2.5 m pixels: the DSM their highest points), so nearly every line is over_trees; at --resolution 1 (bilinear from 2.5 m) the same search finds 295 lines in 6 spots

R31.place: Diorite quarry at Waschenbach (Mühltal) in the Odenwald, Hesse, Germany: HVBG's DGM1 and DOM1 1 m from its rasdaman WCSs (2 km tiles, axes E/N)
R31.notes: --source auto picks hesse (the centre is in DE-HE); first run on an empty cache: 4 tiles of 2 km per layer, 16 MB each, about 1 s per tile; Hesse has few natural cliffs (the Rheingau above Assmannshausen, the Edersee, the Werra valley near Bad Sooden-Allendorf and the Vogelsberg gave 0 lines at radius 400 m): the Odenwald's quarries are its steepest walls (also measured: the basalt quarry of Rossdorf 27225 lines in 315 spots, the quarry of Gross-Bieberau 28688 in 748, Moerlenbach 701 in 30, Neckarsteinach 129 in 6)

R32.place: Königsstuhl in the Jasmund chalk cliffs on Rügen, Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, Germany: LAiV's DGM1 and DOM1 1 m from its MapServer WCSs (2 km tiles, the sea stored as 0 and taken as no data)
R32.notes: --source auto picks mecklenburg_vorpommern (the centre, at the edge of the cliff, is in DE-MV); first run on an empty cache: 4 tiles of 2 km per layer, 16 MB each; the sea (0 in the DGM) is no data and filled as sea (coverage: the land's share of the circle); the DOM holds values near 0 over the sea, not 0; points 1-2 km north and south along the cliffs found 0 lines

R33.place: Sandstone gorges west of Berdorf (Mullerthal climbing area), Luxembourg: ACT's BD-L-Lidar2024 MNT and MNS, 0.5 m blocks of 1 km read by HTTP range requests from the national COGs, averaged onto a 1 m grid in LUREF / Luxembourg TM
R33.notes: --source auto picks luxembourg (the centre is in LU); first run on an empty cache: 4 blocks of 1 km per layer, about 11 MB of float64 read and 6-7 MB cached (float32) each; every line crosses the forest of the gorges (over_trees); also measured (radius 400 m): east of Berdorf (49.8180, 6.3720) 10800 lines in 222 spots, Mullerthal south-west of Berdorf (49.8172, 6.3328) 494 lines in 11 spots, the Sûre at Bourscheid and the Our at Vianden none

R34.place: Mięguszowieckie Szczyty above Morskie Oko, Tatras, Poland: the Slovak side of the border ridge filled from our ÚGKK SR tiles (neighbours across a border)
R34.notes: skipped without FINDALINE_MIRROR (without it the Slovak side comes from FABDEM); --source auto picks geoportal (the centre is in PL); the border ridge: 0.34 km² filled from 2 Slovak DMR/DMP tiles of 2 km, nothing left for FABDEM; geoportal has no NMPT sheet here

R35.place: Inn gorge at Finstermünz, Austria: the Swiss bank filled from swisstopo (neighbours across a border)

R36.place: Brenner pass, South Tyrol (IT-BZ): the Austrian side filled from BEV's ALS DTM and DSM (neighbours across a border)

R37.place: Ecker valley below the Ecker dam, Harz, Lower Saxony: the Saxony-Anhalt bank filled from LVermGeo's DGM1 and DOM1 (neighbours across a border)
R37.notes: --source auto picks lower_saxony (the centre is in DE-NI); the Ecker is the border: 0.05 km² from 1 LVermGeo WCS tile of 2 km (LGLN's tiles reach across the river), 0.04 km² left for FABDEM; the Harz has no crags at the border: few lines

R38.place: Møns Klint, Denmark: Klimadatastyrelsen's DHM/Terræn and DHM/Overflade from Datafordeler's WCS with the server's API key (the sea, stored as 0, taken as no data)
R38.notes: --source auto picks denmark (the centre is in DK); the chalk cliff on the east coast of Møn, 400 m around the source's sample; at 12.5420 (560 m west of the cliff) 0 lines

R39.place: Korouoma canyon, Posio, Finland: NLS's elevation model 2 m, blocks of 2 km read by HTTP range requests from the 6 km TM35 sheets on CSC's Paituli mirror, in ETRS-TM35FIN
R39.notes: --source auto picks finland (the centre is in FI); first run on an empty cache: 4 blocks of 2 km, about 2 MB each; no surface model, so over_trees is never counted; also measured: Korouoma at radius 1500 m 54 lines in 8 spots, Olhavanvuori (Kouvola, 61.1888, 26.8412, radius 600 m), Isokuru (Pyhatunturi, 67.0176, 27.2389, 600 m) and the Kevo canyon (69.7354, 26.9819, 800 m) none; radius 1500 m (the user, 2026-11-01: 600 m gave only 40 lines in 4 spots)

R40.place: Preikestolen, Lysefjord, Norway: Kartverket's NHM DTM 1 / DOM 1 (1 m) from Geonorge's WCS 1.0.0 in ETRS89 / UTM 33N, the sea 0.0 taken as no data
R40.notes: --source auto picks norway (the centre is in NO); first run on an empty cache (with the default --max-length 1000): 4 tiles of 2 km per layer, 7-17 MB each, about 2.5 s a tile; the fjord comes back as 0.0 in the DTM (no data: filled as sea, sea_km2) and as about -0.1 m in the DOM; DOM - DTM is up to about 16 m (p99, forest) with outliers of 100+ m at vertical walls, so most lines are over trees; with the defaults (--max-length 1000) 200601 lines in 693 spots, too many for a quick test: --min-length 50 --max-length 300 (the coordinates are the pulpit rock itself, checked on the map)

R41.place: Stawamus Chief, Squamish, British Columbia, Canada: NRCan's HRDEM national mosaic 1 m (DTM and DSM), blocks of 1 km read by HTTP range requests from its 500 km COGs on AWS, in its own EPSG:3979 (Canada Atlas Lambert, scale -0.26 % here)
R41.notes: --source auto picks canada (the centre is in CA); first run on an empty cache: blocks of 1 km of the 500 km COG 2_4, about 2 MB each; the three peaks of the Chief with the North and South Gully between them (179 spots of lines of 50-400 m); every line crosses the gullies' forest, so over_trees is all of them; gaps (0.3 km2, the creeks and the shore) filled from the 2 m mosaic and MRDEM-30; lengths on EPSG:3979 are 0.26 % short here; also measured: radius 800 m with the default lengths, 36533 lines in 283 spots (30-919 m), 84 s on an empty cache

R42.place: Castle Hill / Kura Tawhiti, Canterbury, New Zealand: LINZ's national 1 m DEM and DSM, blocks of 1 km read by HTTP range requests from the LERC COGs of the Topo50 sheets (BW21) on the nz-elevation bucket, in NZTM2000
R42.notes: --source auto picks new_zealand (the centre is in NZ); first run on an empty cache: 4-6 blocks of 1 km per layer, about 2 MB each; limestone boulders and outcrops of the conservation area; almost every line is marked over trees/buildings: the DSM stands 2-35 m above the DEM on 1-3 % of the blocks' pixels (trees, boulders) and the lines run low over the basin; also measured: radius 800 m, 30-300 m: 3120 lines in 124 spots

R43.place: The Verdon gorge below the Route des Crêtes (Escalès), Alpes-de-Haute-Provence, France: IGN's LiDAR HD MNT / MNS (0.5 m, fetched at 1 m: the exact mean of 2 x 2 pixels) by WMS-R GetMaps in Lambert-93
R43.notes: --source auto picks france (the centre is in FR); first run on an empty cache: 6 tiles of 1 km per layer at 1 m, 2.7-2.9 MB each (DEFLATE), about 1 s a tile; the limestone walls of the gorge's right bank (the steepest pixels of the Escalès area, 300 m below the rim); almost every line is marked over trees: the MNS holds the box trees and pines on the ledges and the rim; the first try at the belvedere's coordinates (43.7655, 6.3580) is on the plateau (41 anchors, no line)

R53.place: Saut du Doubs, the France / Switzerland border: IGN's LiDAR HD on the French bank (and a few hundred metres into Switzerland), swisstopo's swissALTI3D / swissSURFACE3D filling the border gap at the circle's edge (a neighbour), RGE ALTI the holes inside
R53.notes: --source auto picks france (the centre, on the French bank above the Lac des Brenets, is in FR); first run on an empty cache: 9 tiles of 1 km per layer, one without data (Swiss); LiDAR HD reaches a few hundred metres into Switzerland, so swisstopo (the neighbour) fills only the border gap at the edge of the circle (0.02 km2) and RGE ALTI the holes inside it (the lake's surface and the river, 0.12 km2); the cliffs of the Doubs gorge are wooded: every line over trees, 21 over the water

R44.place: Adršpach rock town (Adršpašské skály), Czechia: ČÚZK's DMR 5G and DMP 1G (2 m) from its ArcGIS ImageServers (exportImage) in S-JTSK / Krovak East North

R45.place: Schrammsteine (Lorenzwände), Elbe Sandstone Mountains, Saxony, Germany: GeoSN's DGM1 / DOM1 (1 m), zipped 2 km GeoTIFFs from its Nextcloud share in ETRS89 / UTM 33N
R45.notes: --source auto picks saxony (the centre is in DE-SN); first run on an empty cache: 4 ZIPs of 2 km per layer, about 16 MB each, about 1 s a ZIP; the centre is on the Schrammsteine's sandstone towers south of the Großer Dom gully (the research's 50.920, 14.210 lies in the gully north of them: 2796 lines in 44 spots with r 800, 50-400 m); the towers stand close together, so a narrow search: r 700 with 50-400 m gave 371372 lines in 2303 spots, r 400 with 30-150 m 27674 in 249; nearly every line crosses forest in the gaps between the towers (over_trees); seen on a slope map of the DGM1 with the spots drawn

R46.place: Danube valley at Beuron, Swabian Jura, Baden-Württemberg, Germany: LGL's DGM1 (1 m, four 1 km XYZ grids per 2 km ZIP) and DOM1 (four 1 km GeoTIFFs per ZIP) in ETRS89 / UTM 32N
R46.notes: --source auto picks baden_wurttemberg (the centre is in DE-BW); first run on an empty cache: 6 ZIPs of 2 km per layer (14.5 MB with four 29 MB XYZ grids for the DGM1, 12 MB with four GeoTIFFs for the DOM1), about 1.3 s to read a DGM1 ZIP; the spots are on the limestone cliffs of the Danube's bends east and south-east of Beuron (the spur north of the bend at 48.051-48.055 N, 8.974-8.984 E, the rocks above the river at 48.046 N, 8.977 E and further east), seen on a slope map of the DGM1 with the spots drawn; every line crosses the valley's forest (over_trees)

R47.place: Pottenstein, Franconian Switzerland (Franconian Jura), Bavaria, Germany: LDBV's DGM1 (1 m) and DOM20 (0.2 m, image matching, averaged to 1 m), 1 km GeoTIFFs listed by Metalinks, in ETRS89 / UTM 32N
R47.notes: --source auto picks bavaria (the centre is in DE-BY); first run on an empty cache: the Land's DGM1 Metalink (09.meta4, 4.2 MB gzipped) and the seven DOM20 Metalinks of the Regierungsbezirke (4.4 MB gzipped) asked once and kept, 12 tiles of 1 km per layer: the DGM1 2.7-3.4 MB each, the DOM20 about 49 MB each (0.2 m, averaged 5 x 5 to 1 m, about 0.7 s a tile, 2.2 MB cached); 620 MB in 14 s; the spots are on the dolomite crags of the Püttlach valley around Pottenstein (the biggest groups at 49.770-49.776 N, 11.414-11.422 E, east of the castle, and at 49.769 N, 11.408 E); almost every line crosses forest (over_trees)

R48.place: Dahner Felsenland at Dahn, Palatinate Forest, Rhineland-Palatinate, Germany: LVermGeo RP's DGM1 / DOM1 (1 m, ALS), 1 km GeoTIFFs listed by the Land's Metalinks, in ETRS89 / UTM 32N
R48.notes: --source auto picks rhineland_palatinate (the centre is in DE-RP); first run on an empty cache: the Land's DGM1 and DOM1 Metalinks (12 and 7.6 MB) asked once and kept, 16 tiles of 1 km per layer (1.5-3 MB, survey 2022 here), written in EPSG:25832's name (the DGM1 names a compound CRS with DHHN2016); 73 MB in 4 s; the spots are on the sandstone rocks west of Dahn (49.146-49.153 N, 7.768-7.774 E); every line crosses the forest (over_trees)

R49.place: The Old Man of Hoy and the cliffs of Rackwick, Hoy, Orkney, Scotland: Orkney Islands Council's LiDAR 2023 (DTM / DSM 0.5 m, 1 km GeoTIFFs in the Scottish Remote Sensing Portal's open S3 bucket, listed by ListObjectsV2) in British National Grid
R49.notes: --source auto picks scotland (the centre is in GB-SCT); first run on an empty cache: 9 blocks of 1 km per layer from Orkney 2023's uncompressed files (the national programme does not reach Hoy), 95 MB read with the water mask in 8 s; 72.6 % of the circle is land with data, the rest sea (OSM coastline); the spots are on the Old Man of Hoy (58.884-58.886 N, 3.426-3.431 W) and the cliffs north of it (58.891-58.893 N); --max-length 250 (400 gives 64 780 lines); Cir Mhor on Arran (the national programme) gave 10 lines only

R50.place: Bruchhauser Steine, Sauerland, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany: Geobasis NRW's DGM1 / DOM1 (1 m) from its WCS in ETRS89 / UTM 32N
R50.notes: --source auto picks north_rhine_westphalia (the centre is in DE-NW); first run on an empty cache: 4 WCS tiles of 2 km per layer, 92 MB with the water mask in 4 s; the spots are on the Bruchhauser Steine (Feldstein and Bornstein, 51.323-51.324 N, 8.545-8.546 E) in the forest (over_trees)

R51.place: Monte Colodri above Arco, Sarca valley, Trentino, Italy: the Province of Trento's LiDAR 2014 DTM / DSM (0.5 m, plain ASCII grids of 500 m) in ETRS89 / UTM 32N
R51.notes: --source auto picks trento (the centre is in IT-TN); first run on an empty cache: 25 ASCII grids of 500 m per layer (about 7 MB each), 330 MB in 10 s; the spots are on the Colodri wall and the rocks above Arco (45.926-45.928 N, 10.886-10.889 E)
